name: transcribe-speech
summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass (greedy, English-forced decoding).
description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say'. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong. Does not detect speech presence/absence (see audio.detect-speech-segments for that), translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want spoken audio transcribed to text, so that I can search, summarize, or extract entities from what was said without a separate ASR service.
As a meeting organizer, I want silent or empty audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a hallucinated guess, so that gaps in a recording don't produce fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies up to 480000 (30s) samples of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; fewer than 30s of audio is zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window.

postconditions.description: Empty samples, or audio whose total energy is below a small fixed threshold, yields text="" rather than a hallucinated transcript.
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a text transcript in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input audio.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#473, fifth and final model from this session's AI-WASM-model review, following #455/#460/#465/#469 -- fifth spec 001 FR-017 agent (fourth genuinely model_backed one; text.detect-language/#469 correctly did not qualify). Motivated as a natural complement to audio.detect-speech-segments (#460): speech-presence detection is a short step from transcription, and free-text output feeds directly into text.detect-entities (#465) and text.detect-language (#469) as a pipeline.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/audio-transcribe-speech: 14 #[test] cases (WHSP1 header parse, malformed-table graceful degradation, GELU/LayerNorm/conv1d/sinusoid-embedding math primitives, BPE detokenize incl. special-id exclusion, empty/silent-input -> empty transcript, full pipeline runs without panicking and is deterministic, run() without full-model feature degrades gracefully) against a small structurally-valid synthetic WHSP1 fixture (the fixture's n_audio_ctx is deliberately NOT a free parameter -- it must equal the fixed DSP front end's real conv-computed 1500 timesteps, a genuine integration bug this test caught before publish); cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=98.46%, regions=98.59%. Separately verified end to end against the real published ONNX graphs (Xenova/whisper-tiny onnx/encoder_model.onnx + onnx/decoder_model.onnx) via a from-scratch pure-numpy encoder+decoder implementation (not just calling onnxruntime): matched the onnxruntime baseline token-for-token on a real 11s speech sample (openai/whisper's own tests/jfk.flac fixture, the famous JFK quote) after fixing a real bug caught this way (a forgotten v_proj.bias in the weight-loading dict, silently defaulting to zero and producing a ~17-magnitude hidden-state divergence, invisible without this independent cross-check). Quantization tested (int8 weights incl. the tied embed_tokens table), not assumed: the full greedy autoregressive loop on the same real audio matched the float32 baseline's transcript exactly except for one comma token -- autoregressive token decisions proved robust to per-weight quantization noise, unlike audio.detect-speech-segments' recurrent Silero VAD (registry#460), where int8 measurably broke the LSTM's output. The compiled --features full-model wasm32-unknown-unknown artifact was run under wasmtime (CLI) on the same real audio (both the full 11s clip and a 1s excerpt): output matched the quantized Python reference exactly, byte for byte. Building this artifact against real 176000-sample audio input also surfaced a real bump-allocator OOM (exit(2)) at the prior 64 MiB shared heap ceiling -- not from this capability's own ~41 MiB of audio/attention scratch buffers, but from the shared JSON parser's Vec<Value> being grown by repeated reallocation for a long input array, with every abandoned smaller buffer staying allocated forever in a bump allocator that never frees. Fixed by raising capability-src/wasi-capability-runtime's shared HEAP_SIZE constant 64 -> 192 MiB (same allocator, same zero-cost-headroom rationale as the prior 16->64 MiB raise for registry#384) -- re-ran the full cargo test suite for text.detect-entities, audio.detect-speech-segments, text.detect-language, and report.translate-fr-semantic after the change to confirm no regression from this shared-crate edit. License: dual-attested -- openai/whisper's own GitHub LICENSE file is MIT (verified directly); the openai/whisper-tiny Hugging Face model card's own metadata (cardData.license) says apache-2.0. Both primary sources, both permissive; logged as-is.
